Key M = major · m = minor · X = double · XX = redouble · P = pass · (2♥) = opponents' bid · HCP = high-card points · GF = game forcing · NF = non-forcing · Tier 0 every session · Tier 1 most sessions · Tier 2 occasional

Opening bids Tier 0

Opening Meaning
1♣ 3+ clubs, 12–21. With 3-3 in the minors open 1♣
1♦ 4+ diamonds (3 only with exactly 4♠ 4♥ 3♦ 2♣). With 4-4 in the minors open 1♦
1♥ / 1♠ 5+ cards, 12–21. With 5-5 open the higher suit
1NT 15–17 balanced. May hold a 5-card major
2♣ Strong, artificial: 22+ HCP or about 9 tricks
2♦ / 2♥ / 2♠ Weak two: 6 cards, 5–10 HCP
2NT 20–21 balanced
3-level Preempt, about 7 cards
3NT Gambling: solid 7+ card minor (AKQxxxx), little outside
4-level Preempt, about 8 cards

Light openings: 1st and 2nd seat use the Rule of 20 (HCP + cards in two longest suits ≥ 20). 3rd seat may open about 10 HCP with a good suit. 4th seat: always open with 14+ HCP; with 9–13 HCP open only if the Rule of 15 holds (HCP + number of spades ≥ 15).

Which suit: longest first. 5-5 → higher. 6-5 → longer, then bid the other twice.

Responding to 1♥ / 1♠ Tier 0

Response Meaning
1♠ (over 1♥) 4+ spades, 6+ HCP
1NT Forcing one round, 6–12. May hide a 3-card limit raise
New suit at 2-level 2/1: game forcing, 12+. 1♠–2♥ promises 5+ hearts. 2♣ may be 3 cards
2M 6–9 dummy points, 3+ trumps
1NT, then 3M 3-card limit raise, 10–12
3M 4-card limit raise, 10–12
2NT Jacoby: 4+ trumps, 13+ dummy points, game forcing
Single jump in new suit Weak jump shift: 6+ cards, 2–5 HCP
Double jump in new suit Splinter: 4+ trumps, singleton/void there, 10–14 HCP (1♥–3♠/4♣/4♦, 1♠–4♣/4♦)
4M Preemptive: 5+ trumps, weak

Jacoby 2NT, opener's replies: 3 new suit = singleton/void · 4 new suit = good 5-card side suit · 3M = 18+, no shortness · 3NT = 15–17 · 4M = minimum.

After 1M–2M: new suit = help-suit game try · 3M = general invite.

Opener after 1M–1NT: cheapest 3-card minor with a balanced minimum (2♣ may be 3 cards) · 2M = 6+ minimum · 2NT = 18–19 · 3M = 6+ good, 16–18.

2/1 is off for a passed hand and in competition (then a new suit is forcing one round only).

Responding to 1♣ / 1♦ Tier 0

Response Meaning
1♥ / 1♠ 4+ cards. 4-4 → bid the cheaper (up the line). 5-4 → longer first
Over 1♣ with < 12 HCP Skip diamonds to show a 4-card major (Walsh)
1NT 6–10, no 4-card major
2NT 11–12 balanced, no 4-card major, invitational
3NT 13–15 balanced, no 4-card major
1♦–2♣ 2/1 game forcing
2m raise Inverted: 10+, forcing, no 4-card major (Tier 1)
3m raise Weak, preemptive, 5–9
Single jump in new suit Weak jump shift
Double jump in new suit Splinter for opener's minor, game forcing

A 1♠ response denies 4 hearts unless it shows 5+ spades.

Opener's rebids Tier 0

Rebid Meaning
1NT 12–14 balanced
2NT (jump) 18–19 balanced
Raise responder's major to 2 12–15, 4 trumps (rarely 3 with a ruffing value)
Jump raise to 3 16–18, 4 trumps
Raise to 4 19–20, 4 trumps
Jump rebid of own suit 16–18, 6+ cards, invitational
Reverse (e.g. 1♦–1♠–2♥) 16+, first suit longer, forcing one round
Jump shift 19+, game forcing
Double jump / jump reverse Splinter: 4-card support, about 18+

After a reverse, responder: 2NT = weak, forces 3♣, then pass or sign off · rebid own suit = 5+, forcing one round · anything else = game forcing.

After a 2/1 game-forcing response a "reverse" shows shape only, no extra strength.

Fast arrival: in a game-forcing auction, jumping to game shows the weakest hand.

Notrump bidding Tier 0

After 1NT Meaning
2♣ Stayman (garbage Stayman allowed)
2♦ / 2♥ Transfer to ♥ / ♠
2♠ Puppet to 3♣: pass (clubs) or 3♦ (diamonds), weak
2NT Invitational, 8–9
3♣ / 3♦ Good 6-card minor, invites 3NT
3♥ / 3♠ 3♠ = both minors, slam interest (proposed) · 3♥ not used
3NT To play
4♣ Gerber (only directly over 1NT / 2NT)
4♦ / 4♥ Texas transfer to 4♥ / 4♠, sign-off
4NT Quantitative, invites 6NT

Stayman follow-ups: 1NT–2♣–2♦–2♥/2♠ = 5 cards in that major + 4 in the other, invitational · 1NT–2♣–2♥–2♠ = 4♠, invitational · 1NT–2♣–2♥–3NT = 4♠, game (opener corrects to 4♠ with 4).

Transfer follow-ups: opener super-accepts (jumps to 3M) with 4 trumps and 17 · then 2NT = 5-card invite · 3M = 6-card invite · 3NT = choice of games with 5 · transfer then 4NT = quantitative · Texas then 4NT = RKCB.

5-5 majors: weak → transfer to ♠, pass · invite → 2♦, then 2♠ · game force → 2♥, then 3♥.

2NT opening: same structure one level higher: 3♣ Stayman, 3♦/3♥ transfers, 3♠ = both minors with slam interest, 4♣ Gerber, 4♦/4♥ Texas.

If they interfere over our 1NT: they double → systems on, XX = we have the balance of strength · artificial overcall → X "steals" their bid (X of 2♣ = Stayman), rest systems on · natural overcall → Lebensohl (Tier 2).

Weak twos Tier 0

Opening: 6 cards, 5–10 HCP. In 1st/2nd seat, no 4-card side major and no void.

Responses: new suit = forcing one round · raise = preemptive, to play · 2NT = Ogust.

Ogust reply Strength Suit
3♣ Minimum Bad
3♦ Minimum Good
3♥ Maximum Bad
3♠ Maximum Good
3NT Solid suit (AKQ)

Good suit = 2 of the top 3 honors. Minor replies = minimum, major replies = maximum; the lower of each pair = bad suit.

Tier 1 conventions Tier 1

Convention Summary
Inverted minors 1m–2m = 10+, forcing, no 4-card major · 1m–3m = weak. Opener: 2NT = 12–14, 3NT = 18–19, new suit = stopper, 3m = minimum. Off in competition
XYZ After three 1-level bids (or a 1NT rebid): 2♣ forces 2♦ (sign-off or invite), 2♦ = artificial GF, 2NT = puppet to 3♣, other 2-level bids weak, 3-level jumps GF
Fourth suit forcing Responder bids the 4th suit at the 2-level or higher = artificial, game forcing
Drury P–1♥/1♠–2♣ = 3+ trumps, 10–11. Opener: 2M = light, stop · 4M or anything else = full opening (6 cards with 11–12, or 7+ cards with 9+, bid 4M). On after a double, off after an overcall
Jordan 2NT 1-suit–(X)–2NT = 4+ trumps, limit raise or better · 3M = preemptive · 2M = weak raise
DONT vs 1NT X = one long suit (partner relays 2♣) · 2♣ = ♣ + higher · 2♦ = ♦ + major · 2♥ = ♥ + ♠ · 2♠ = spades. Used against every 1NT
RKCB 1430 5♣ = 1 or 4 · 5♦ = 0 or 3 · 5♥ = 2 no Q · 5♠ = 2 + Q · next step = queen ask · 5NT = kings by number (all key cards held)

Slam extras: If they bid over 4NT: X = 0 or 3, P = 1 or 4, next step = 2. If they double 4NT: XX = 0 or 3, P = 1 or 4. Voids are not shown. Gerber replies: 4♦ = 0/4, 4♥ = 1, 4♠ = 2, 4NT = 3, 5♣ asks kings. Control bids: cheapest first- or second-round control, up the line.

Tier 2 conventions Tier 2

Convention Summary
Support X / XX Opener's X (or XX after their double) = exactly 3-card support for responder's major. Raise = 4. On through 2 of responder's suit
Smolen 1NT–2♣–2♦–3♥ = 4♥ + 5♠ · 3♠ = 4♠ + 5♥, game forcing. Opener bids the 5-card major with 3, else 3NT
Lebensohl After 1NT–(2-level overcall): 2-level = to play · 2NT forces 3♣, then sign-off (or invite above their suit) · direct 3-level = GF · cue or 3NT: direct denies a stopper, via 2NT shows one. Same 2NT relay after a reverse and after partner doubles a weak two
2♣ opening 2♦ waiting · 2♥/2♠/3♣/3♦ = good 5+ suit, 8+ · 2NT = 8+ balanced. Opener: 2NT = 22–24, 3NT = 25–27 (systems on). Second negative (0–3) = 3♣; 3♦ over 3♣; 3♥ over 3♦. GF except 2NT and after a second negative

Watch out Tier 0

  • 4♣ is Gerber only directly over partner's 1NT or 2NT (including 2♣–2♦–2NT). Everywhere else 4♣ is natural or a splinter.
  • 4NT is RKCB only when a suit is agreed. After notrump bidding with no agreed suit, 4NT is quantitative.
  • A reverse after a 2/1 response shows no extra strength.
  • 1♠ over a minor denies 4 hearts unless spades are 5+.
  • Inverted minors and 2/1 are off in competition.
  • Drury and 2/1 depend on a passed hand: P–1♠–2♣ is Drury, never a game force.
